hypothesis: Fourfold boundary weighting was better than onefold, twofold, or eightfold weighting. Threefold weighting tests whether combining intermediate and final temporal scales better explains the remaining spatial instruction patterns.

pcvs.name: latent_volume
pcvs.rationale: Captures spatial-volume work common to both cache regimes.

pcvs.expression: x.shape[0] * x.shape[2] * x.shape[3] * x.shape[4] if feat_cache is not None and feat_cache[feat_idx[0]] is not None else 0
pcvs.name: cached_latent_volume
pcvs.rationale: Allows an independent volume slope for cached execution.

pcvs.expression: int(feat_cache is not None and feat_cache[feat_idx[0]] is not None)
pcvs.name: has_cached_features
pcvs.rationale: Captures fixed overhead from cache handling and temporal operations.

pcvs.expression: x.shape[0] * x.shape[2] * (x.shape[3] + x.shape[4]) * (3 if feat_cache is not None and feat_cache[feat_idx[0]] is not None else 1)
pcvs.name: mixed_stage_boundary
pcvs.rationale: Approximates combined boundary work across stages with onefold, twofold, and fourfold temporal extent.
